indicators: Chevron company records document patches of green algae near its first drilling rigs.
impact_on_santa_rosa: An early biological precedent of the cyanobacteria that, a century later, would overwhelm the shores of Santa Rosa.

indicators: After the Barroso II well blowout (1922), intensive installation of wells and underwater pipelines begins across the basin.
impact_on_santa_rosa: First traces of hydrocarbons carried by currents towards the north of the lake and the stilt-house shores.

indicators: The Lake Maracaibo navigation channel is opened and deepened so that large tankers can pass.
impact_on_santa_rosa: Massive inflow of salt water from the Gulf of Venezuela upset the estuarine balance, displacing freshwater species traditionally fished locally.

event: Urban growth without sanitation, and oil spills
indicators: An historical average of 15 spills per month is recorded in the lake, while Maracaibo grows without sewage treatment plants.
impact_on_santa_rosa: More than 100 city drainage channels start discharging sewage and waste directly onto the northern shore and the Capitán Chico mangrove.

event: Creation of ICLAM and health alerts
indicators: The Institute for the Control and Conservation of the Lake Maracaibo Basin (ICLAM) is founded to monitor the ecological crisis.
impact_on_santa_rosa: The first bacteriological samples detect critical levels of faecal coliforms, restricting recreational use of northern Maracaibo's beaches.

indicators: Sustained build-up of nitrogen and phosphorus in the water; urban landfill expands over coastal wetlands.
impact_on_santa_rosa: The protective fringe of red mangrove (Rhizophora mangle) shrinks, making the stilt houses more vulnerable to waves.

indicators: An explosive bloom of Lemna aequinoctialis and Lemna obscura covered 14–15% of the lake (1,870 km² and 93 million m³).
impact_on_santa_rosa: Artisanal fishing stops completely, boats are blocked, fish die from anoxia and neighbours protest over foul smells.

event: Recurring Lemna cycles and heavy metals
indicators: Every year between May and September duckweed mats return; studies detect lead, nickel, chromium and arsenic in the plant biomass.
impact_on_santa_rosa: Restaurants on the tourist boulevard close temporarily during decomposition peaks, and families lose income.

event: Assessment of declining quality of life
indicators: Postgraduate research at Universidad Rafael Urdaneta (URU) documents the accelerated destruction of the mangrove in Santa Rosa.
impact_on_santa_rosa: A direct link is confirmed between wetland degradation, more disease vectors and the socio-economic decline of residents.

event: Creation of the Tierra de Sueños Community Park
indicators: 130 hectares of mangrove are delimited in the Punta Capitán Chico sector to try to stop deforestation and illegal landfill.
impact_on_santa_rosa: Despite the protected status, the ecosystem keeps receiving untreated sewage from neighbouring homes.

event: Collapse of oil infrastructure and chronic waste
indicators: More than 10,000 abandoned or unmaintained oil installations leak crude continuously; urban waste collection in Maracaibo fails.
impact_on_santa_rosa: Plastic and oil cover up to 90% of the shoreline. Clean-ups remove 600 kg of waste in just 3 hours without stopping the flow.

indicators: Torrential rain and rising lake levels flood more than 200 stilt and coastal homes in Santa Rosa de Agua.
impact_on_santa_rosa: When the water receded, tonnes of plastic, glass, metal and crude oil were left trapped among the piles and roots.

indicators: Environmental organisations document between 22 and 32 major spills in Lake Maracaibo over the year.
impact_on_santa_rosa: Fishers report nets ruined by tar and fish soaked in hydrocarbons that cannot be sold or eaten.

indicators: A massive bloom of the toxic microalga Microcystis along the whole northern shore; the Lake Rescue Master Plan is activated.
impact_on_santa_rosa: Tourism and food trade in Santa Rosa fall by 25%. Outbreaks of asthma, allergies and skin rashes are reported in children and fishers.

indicators: The Ministry of Ecosocialism reports thousands of clean-up days, but crude patches and cyanobacteria persist in hot periods.
impact_on_santa_rosa: Media such as Crónica Uno document the progressive abandonment of businesses at the tourist pier because of the stench and the look of the water.

event: Environmental emergency in the mangroves and low productivity
indicators: Solid waste keeps washing down the drainage channels in the rains, and people are reported lost in dense areas of the Capitán Chico mangrove.
impact_on_santa_rosa: The community's roughly 1,200 fishers must travel ever further from the estuary to find areas free of crude and verdín.

event: Beach assessments and new oil spills
indicators: In February, ICLAM assesses the Santa Rosa de Agua beach under Decree 883. In August, September and October new crude spills are reported on the shores of Maracaibo and 6 municipalities of Zulia.
impact_on_santa_rosa: The treatment plants announced in 2023 are still not operating, so the water remains polluted by a mix of oil, verdín and sewage.
